description.value: A pilot fMRI study examined neural responses to e-cigarette and neutral cue videos in experienced e-cigarette users before and after e-cigarette use.

spans.text: We sought to bridge this gap by developing a novel set of e-cigarette (salient) and electronic toothbrush (neutral) videos for use in cue-reactivity paradigms.

description.value: Within-participant pre-use and post-use fMRI sessions were conducted in seven experienced e-cigarette users.

spans.text: In this study, participants viewed half of the stimulus videos (both types intermixed) in the MRI while abstinent from nicotine for at least 14 h, provided blood samples while using their e-cigarette, and then viewed the other half of the videos in the MRI.

instructions.value: Participants watched intermixed e-cigarette and electronic toothbrush videos in the MRI while abstinent from nicotine, then used their own e-cigarette and watched the remaining videos after use. Participants were instructed to remain abstinent from e-cigarettes and other nicotine-containing products for 14 hours before the visit.

spans.text: Participants were instructed to remain abstinent from traditional cigarettes for 4 days and from their e-cigarettes (or other nicotine containing products) and caffeine for 14 h prior to the lab visit.

stimuli.value: Twelve 30-second e-cigarette videos depicting actors using first-generation e-cigarettes and twelve 30-second neutral electronic-toothbrush videos, filmed in matched poses against a gray background.

The BrainVoyager QX Cluster-Level Statistical Threshold Estimator plug-in (which implements a Monte-Carlo simulation approach to multiple comparisons correction) was used to determine the appropriate threshold for group statistical maps ( ).

After 1000 iterations, it was determined that a corrected map-wise false positive rate of p < .05 would be obtained by combining a per-voxel threshold of p < .005 with cluster-extent thresholds of 11, 11, and 13 contiguous voxels for the statistical maps corresponding to the main effect of video condition, the main effect of session, and the video condition by session interaction, respectively.
